title: Empty meter can end the run WON: the lose check is gated on !h.won and evaluated after the win check
detail: On the tick the meter first drains to 0 while the surge ends with ≥ threshold window uptime, Ev_Run_Won fires first and the lose check's !h.won gate suppresses Ev_Run_Lost forever — contradicting §6.5 "empty meter → Error 404, run over" and the code's own E17 comment.
recommended_fix: Evaluate the empty-meter condition before the win check (or drop the !h.won gate) so meter 0 always ends as Error 404, per E17.

title: E9 drop ladder (Best→Standard→Express) is not implemented; per-lane queue-depth shedding can drop the premium lane first
detail: The only contention drop is per-lane newest-first shedding; there is no Best→Standard→Express ladder anywhere in advance(). On an emphasized pipe the Express lane (streaming) hits the 60-deep bound first and sheds premium packets while Best (email) waits — inverting §11.7 E9 "Drop ladder BE → Standard → Express".
recommended_fix: When a lane exceeds queue_drop_depth, shed waiting Best-lane packets before Express-lane packets (class ladder), matching the E9 contract.

title: Packets traverse multiple pipes per tick: same-tick spawn→deliver with 0 accrued latency; traversal speed depends on pipe slot order
detail: Pipes serve in slot order; a packet completing edge k is re-served on edge k+1 the same tick, so short uncongested routes spawn-and-deliver in one tick with 0 accrued latency (accrual skips done packets). Traversal speed is pipe-slot-order-dependent and avg_latency undercounts hops.
recommended_fix: Serve each packet at most one edge per tick (track per-packet edge completion in the pipe loop) so latency accrues ≥ 1 tick per hop.

title: E25 'modifiers in the save header from day one' not honored: ODN-11 log header has no modifiers field
evidence:
w_u32(&w, LOG_MAGIC)
	w_u32(&w, LOG_VERSION)
	w_u64(&w, state.seed)
	w_u8(&w, state.era)
	w_u64(&w, state.catalogs.hash)
	w_i32(&w, state.catalogs.balance.logic_hz)
	w_u32(&w, u32(len(state.action_log)))
detail: E25: "Run descriptor carries `modifiers` — in the save header from day one". The header (magic, version, seed, era, catalog_hash, logic_hz) has no modifiers slot; adding it later forces a LOG_VERSION bump and breaks old logs.
recommended_fix: Add a modifiers u8/u16 field to the header and Log_Header/log_read now, per E25.

title: Stale default_budget field from the REMOVED budget system remains in balance.json
detail: Leftover of the budget system replaced by the hardware inventory (0b92fa4); nothing reads it and the loader silently accepts unknown keys, so it rots — the same stale-budget class r1 flagged in draw_and_reject.dem. Balance numbers are single-source (ODN-5).
recommended_fix: Remove default_budget from balance.json and audit data/*.json for other budget leftovers.

title: Demand source_role/sink_role are not fail-fast validated: unknown role strings silently become .None
detail: Unlike class_id (which aborts on "unknown class"), a typo'd role parses to .None with no error; the entry then matches no terminals and all its demand silently accrues as E28 unmet losses — ODN-5 "cross-reference errors abort with a named error" bypassed.
recommended_fix: Validate source_role/sink_role at load like class_id: unknown role → Catalog_Error, fail-fast.

title: Capacity-based smart LB ships in PROTO (canon §6.1 pins PROTO to round-robin) and its semantics aren't the GDD's proportional split
detail: Canon §6.1: "LB modes: round-robin (PROTO) / bandwidth-aware weighted ([LATER] unlock)" — but the boot router_mid (lb_mode_capable: true) activates capacity picking now. And greedy highest-capacity isn't GDD M1's "split proportional to pipe tier" either. Shipped behavior matches neither spec.
recommended_fix: Pin PROTO junctions to round-robin per canon §6.1, or implement the GDD's proportional split and surface the scope change.

title: json.Object (map) iteration in core catalog load — ODN-10 'no map iteration in core'; lint gate 3's regex misses it
detail: ODN-10: "Never iterate a map in core (map order unspecified) — arrays/slices/#soa only; maps are lookup-only". Harmless today only because every consumer is commutative (indexed assignment; grant items summed) and tools/lint.sh gate 3 greps for `map|_by_id|_by_` which json.Object misses. A future non-commutative use is a silent determinism hazard.
recommended_fix: Sort the json.Object keys (or decode entries as arrays) before resolving starting_inventory/grants so iteration order is explicit.
